figures.finding: Full age in New Zealand is twenty, under the Age of Majority Act 1970 (layer 3 has no New Zealand row).
figures.applies: Everyone. Contracts are governed by their own age of eighteen (see minorsContracts). The Act's own text could not be read: legislation.govt.nz answered with an AWS WAF challenge and NZLII with a Cloudflare challenge, so this rests on a law firm quoting the Act.

sources.said: According to the Age of Majority Act 1970, the age at which a person is legally recognised as an adult in New Zealand is 20 years old.

figures.finding: A contract by anyone under eighteen is unenforceable against the minor unless a court finds it fair and reasonable, and is fully binding if the District Court approves it before it is made; the screen agreement for actors is signed by a parent or guardian for an artist under eighteen.

value.binding: District Court approval before the contract (CCLA 2017 s 98), on application by the minor, another party or a guardian (s 99)
value.otherwise: unenforceable against the minor but otherwise effective (s 86); the court may enforce it if fair and reasonable (ss 87-88)
value.industry: SPADA/Equity Individual Performance Agreement: parent or legal guardian signs on behalf of and guarantees an artist under 18

figures.applies: The Act covers every contract, so writing, directing and producing deals as well as performing. The Act was read in the reprint as at 14 July 2017 (hosted by an insurer, the official site being bot-checked); later amendments are not read. No set-aside of earnings was found (blocker).

sources.said: minor means a person who is under the age of 18 years, and a person is of full age if he or she has reached the age of 18 years
Every contract entered into by a minor is unenforceable against the minor but otherwise has effect as if the minor were of full age.
Every contract entered into by a minor has effect as if the minor were of full age if, before the contract is entered into by the minor, it is approved under this section by the District Court.
Where the Artist is under the age of 18 at the time of signature on this Agreement, their parent or legal guardian (not the Agent) must sign below:

figures.finding: No permit is required; the hours come from the producers' and actors' agreement: up to 8 years 6 hours door to door, 9 to 11 years 8 hours door to door, 12 to 16 years 10 hours plus travel, at most 5 days a week, a 12-hour overnight break, a chaperone, and 10 hours of schoolwork a week on long engagements; anyone 15 or under works only outside school hours and not 10pm to 6am.

night.except: with the parent's or guardian's agreement (ScreenSafe)

value.chaperone: a primary-duty chaperone; two if 5 or more children, ratio never below 1:4
value.law: outside school hours only for those 15 or under (Education and Training Act 2020); not 10pm-6am (Health and Safety at Work regulations, Part 4)

figures.applies: The agreement binds productions using it (NZ feature film and television drama) and covers the Artist, a performer; nothing found extends the hours rules to a young writer or director, who falls only under the general school-hours and night rules.

sources.said: a Child Artist is a child when they are under 16 years of age during any of the Pre-Production or Principal Photography Dates of the Production.
Up to and including 8 year olds 6 hours door to door (includes travel time) 9 to 11 year olds 8 hours door to door (includes travel time) 12 to 16 years 10 hours working plus travel

The Artist will work no more than 5 consecutive days, and no more than 5 days in a calendar week) 5. The Child Artist will have at least a 12 hour overnight break (i.e. turnaround), exclusive of travel time.
On long term engagements, the Producer will ensure that the Child Artist is allocated 10 hours per working week for schoolwork (exclusive of production days off).

Children under the age of 16-years-old should not work between the hours of 10pm and 6am. However, if required, work may be undertaken during these hours in consultation with, and if agreed to, by the child's parent or guardian.

If you hire any school-aged students who are 15 years old or under, their work hours must: be outside of school hours only (this is an education requirement) not be between 10pm and 6am (this is a health and safety requirement).

figures.finding: Employment New Zealand names no minimum age for work; for anyone 15 or under it sets only that work is outside school hours (unless the Ministry of Education's exemption certificate) and not between 10pm and 6am.
figures.applies: Every employee. That the law sets no general minimum age is a reading of the agency's page, not a statement found (blocker).

sources.said: You do not have to meet this restriction if you have a certificate of exemption.

figures.finding: Equity New Zealand admits young performers under 17 at a reduced fee (NZ$101.66 a year in 2026); DEGANZ (directors and editors) has a student tier for full-time tertiary students and states no age.

DEGANZ.student: full-time student at a NZ tertiary institution

figures.applies: Performers (Equity NZ) and directors (DEGANZ). The New Zealand Writers Guild's rules were not reached (blocker).

sources.said: Young performers (under 17) pay a further reduced amount.
Young performer (under 17 years) One $1.96 $3.91 $7.82 $101.66
Student Member If you are a FULLTIME student at a NZ tertiary institution.

figures.finding: The New Zealand Film Commission's feature development funding is open to an experienced New Zealand filmmaker who is a citizen or permanent resident; no age or capacity rule is stated.

NZFC.who: experienced New Zealand filmmaker; New Zealand citizen or permanent resident

figures.applies: Feature film development funding page. The fund guideline PDFs refused this environment (S3 AccessDenied), so other funds' rules are not read.

sources.said: Who can apply You can apply if: You are an experienced New Zealand filmmaker The filmmaker is a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident

figures.finding: A person under eighteen cannot be a company director.
figures.applies: Companies registered under the Companies Act 1993 (the Companies Office cites the Act; its s 151 text was not read, the legislation site being bot-checked).

sources.said: Some of the reasons you cannot be a director include if you are: under 18 years of age

figures.finding: The New Zealand Writers Guild sets no age: it admits by credits or screenwriting earnings for full tiers, and as associates writers not yet produced who are students (with a current student ID) or unwaged.

NZWG.fullTiers: by screen credits and earnings (A+ more than 50 minutes of credits or over $50,000 earned in the previous year)
NZWG.associateStudent: a writer not yet produced, with a current student ID
